175:949.name: Type=Font
175:949.description: SwiftUI: Type=Font → Label(_, systemImage:), symbol name in the Symbol property. Type=Image → Label(_, image:) / Image(“name”) from Assets.xcassets (PNG or PDF). Drill into the nested “Swatch” layer for its own Icon property (currently Blue/Gray test placeholders, default Gray -- replace with real assets via “Your Icons” on page “1.3. Assets”). Pre-size 28x28pt -- .resizable()/.frame() unavailable on tab items. Switch Type on this instance first. Symbol lives on the nested Icon layer: Figma never forwards a nested TEXT property up as an own property, so an ancestor can only reach it if every instance in the chain is marked as an exposed nested instance. That chain is already wired for buttons — Button exposes Label, Label exposes Leading and Trailing Icon — so Symbol is editable straight from a Toolbar or Button instance.

181:1885.name: _Avatar
181:1885.description:
A contact picture. App-drawn — Contacts draws its own; in your app this is a clipped `Circle` view.

• Placeholder — no picture: a person glyph on the monogram gradient, as Messages shows it.
• Monogram — initials on the gradient, `Miscellaneous/Avatar/Monogram Top/Bottom` (measured).
• Image — a photo: `Image(…).resizable().scaledToFill().clipShape(.circle)`.
• Emoji — Contacts allows an emoji picture; not seen in Messages on Mobbin, modelled on request.
• Group — two overlapping pictures for a group conversation.

Size — Small 28 beside bubbles in a group thread, Medium 46 in the conversation list, Large 56 in the conversation header, Extra Large 80 on contact details (all measured off Messages on Mobbin). Initials and emoji are properties.

175:948.name: _Icon Slot
175:948.description:
Icon slot with three content types, matching how images reach an iOS view:

- Type=Font → SF Symbol. In code: Image(systemName: “star.fill”) or Label(_, systemImage:). Size is driven by .font()/.imageScale(), which is why the glyph here is bound to a font-size variable rather than the frame -- resizing the frame alone will not enlarge a symbol.
- Type=Icon → a vector asset you ship (SVG/PDF in Assets.xcassets). In code: Image(“name”), usually with .renderingMode(.template) so it takes the tint color. Scales with the frame.
- Type=Image → a raster asset (PNG). In code: Image(“name”).resizable().scaledToFill() -- note .resizable() is required or the image ignores the frame entirely. Scales with the frame.

All three scale when you resize the slot, except the SF Symbol glyph itself: Figma cannot scale a glyph via constraints, and the glyph sits inside this instance so its constraints cannot be overridden. Change the icon’s font-size variable instead.

Note for tab bars specifically: pre-size assets to 28x28pt -- .resizable()/.frame() are not available on tab items, so the asset must already be the right size.
